paper_metadata.title: Heterostructure and twinning driven enhancement of strength and ductility in CoCrFeNi HEA at the cryogenic temperature

evidence.quote: The quaternary equiatomic CoCrFeNi high-entropy alloy (HEA) with a face-centered cubic (FCC) structure exhibits significant strengthening and strain hardening at cryogenic temperatures

The equiatomic CoCrFeNi HEA was prepared by vacuum induction melting, producing 6 mm thick ingots with a purity exceeding 99.9%.
The ingots were homogenized in vacuum at 1100 °C for 24 h and followed by air cooling.
Then these ingots were subsequently processed into thin sheets of 1 mm thickness through multiple rolling passes, achieving an 83 % reduction in thickness.

evidence.section: 4.1 Enhanced mechanical incompatibility at low temperature

evidence.quote: the ratio of HDI stress σ HDI to the overall flow stress σ f in the HS sample shows a steady increase from 0.56 to 0.62 with strain
The heterostructure leverages a distinct strain partitioning mechanism to maximize hetero-deformation-induced (HDI) strengthening and strain hardening.

The HDI effect is amplified at the cryogenic temperature, promoting deformation twinning and further enhancing strain hardening capacity

The strength disparity between different zones leads to progressive yielding, resulting in pronounced zonal heterogeneity in plastic deformation between the RZs (CG + FG zones) and NRZs, namely strain partitioning

The resulting strain gradients at HBs promote the accumulation of GNDs, which generates long-range internal stresses — back stress in soft zones and forward stress in hard zones — contributing to HDI hardening
